Volume 265 Biographies 24: Li Fang, Lu Mengzheng, Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong

1
李昉，字明遠，深州饒陽人。 父起，晉工部郎中、集賢殿直學士。 從大父右資善大夫超無子，以昉為後，蔭補齋郎，選授太子校書。 漢乾祐舉進士，為秘書郎。 宰相馮道引之，與呂端同直弘文館，改右拾遺、集賢殿修撰。
Li Fang, whose style was Mingyuan, came from Raoyang in Shenzhou. His father Qi had served as Director in the Ministry of Works of Jin and as Academician-Attendant of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. His great-uncle on his father's side, the Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent Chao, had no children, so Fang was adopted as his heir; through yin privilege he was made a Chamberlain's Aide, and by examination he was selected as Crown Prince's Proofreader. In the Qianyou reign of Later Han he earned his jinshi degree and was appointed Secretary Gentleman. Chief Minister Feng Dao brought him forward; he served in the Hongwen Institute alongside Lü Duan, then was promoted to Right Reminder and Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
2
周顯德二年，宰相李穀征淮南，昉為記室。 世宗覽軍中章奏，愛其辭理明白，已知為昉所作，及見《相國寺文英院集》，乃昉與扈蒙、崔頌、劉袞、竇儼、趙逢及昉弟載所題，益善昉詩而稱賞之曰：「吾久知有此人矣。 」師還，擢為主客員外郎、知制誥、集賢殿直學士。 四年，加史館修撰、判館事。 是年冬，世宗南征，從至高郵，會陶穀出使，內署書詔填委，乃命為屯田郎中、翰林學士。 六年春，丁內艱。 恭帝嗣位，賜金紫。
In the second year of Xiande of Later Zhou, when Chief Minister Li Gu marched against Huainan, Fang served on his staff as recorder. Emperor Shizong read through the army's memorials, admired their lucid argument, and already knew Fang had written them; when he came upon the Collected Writings of the Wenyuan Court of Xiangguo Temple—works by Fang together with Hu Meng, Cui Song, Liu Gun, Dou Yan, Zhao Feng, and Fang's younger brother Zai—he admired Fang's poetry all the more and exclaimed, "I have known of this man for a long time. " After the army returned he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions, given charge of drafting edicts, and made Academician-Attendant of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. In the fourth year he was further appointed Compiler of the Historiography Institute and put in charge of its affairs. That winter, when the emperor campaigned south, Fang accompanied him as far as Gaoyou; Tao Gu was sent abroad on a mission, and with edicts flooding the inner secretariat Fang was appointed Director of the Bureau of State Farms and Hanlin Academician. In the spring of the sixth year he entered mourning for his mother. When Emperor Gong took the throne, Fang was awarded the gold-and-purple insignia of high office.
3
宋初，加中書舍人。 建隆三年，罷為給事中。 四年，平湖湘，受詔祀南嶽，就命知衡州，逾年代歸。 陶穀誣奏昉為所親求京畿令，上怒，召吏部尚書張昭面質其事。 昭老儒氣直，免冠上前，抗聲云：「穀罔上。 」上疑之不釋，出昉為彰武軍行軍司馬，居延州，為生業以老。 三歲當內徙，昉不願。 宰相薦其可大用，開寶二年，召還，復拜中書舍人。 未幾，直學士院。 三年，知貢舉。 五年，復知貢舉。 秋，預宴大明殿，上見昉坐盧多遜下，因問宰相，對曰：「多遜學士，昉直殿爾。 」即令真拜學士，令居多遜上。 昉之知貢舉也，其鄉人武濟川預選，既而奏對失次，昉坐左遷太常少卿，俄判國子監。 明年五月，復拜中書舍人、翰林學士。 冬，判吏部銓。 時趙普為多遜所構，數以其短聞於上，上詢於昉，對曰：「臣職司書詔，普之所為，非臣所知。 」普尋出鎮，多遜遂參知政事。
At the founding of the Song dynasty he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter. In the third year of Jianlong he was demoted to Supervising Censor. In the fourth year, after pacifying Hunan, he received orders to perform sacrifices at the Southern Marchmount and was appointed on the spot to govern Hengzhou; he returned home after a year in office. Tao Gu lodged a false accusation that Fang had sought a capital-district magistracy for a protégé; the emperor was furious and summoned Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhao to question him in person. Zhao, an old scholar of blunt integrity, doffed his cap and stepped forward, declaring in a ringing voice, "Gu has deceived Your Majesty. " The emperor's suspicions did not lift; Fang was sent out as Military Administrator of the Zhangwu Army and lived at Yanzhou, supporting himself in retirement. After three years he was due for an inward transfer, but Fang declined. The chief minister recommended him as fit for greater use; in the second year of Kaibao he was recalled and again made Secretariat Drafter. Shortly afterward he was assigned to the Academy of Scholars. In the third year he was put in charge of the civil examinations. In the fifth year he again oversaw the civil examinations. That autumn, at a banquet in the Hall of Great Brightness, the emperor noticed Fang seated below Lu Duosun and asked the chief minister why; the reply was, "Duosun is a full academician; Fang only attends the hall. " The emperor immediately ordered Fang formally invested as academician and given the seat above Duosun. When Fang ran the examinations, his fellow townsman Wu Jichuan was among the candidates; later, in a palace audience, Wu lost his composure, and Fang was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon put in charge of the Directorate of Education. The following May he was again made Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician. That winter he was assigned to oversee personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel. At that time Zhao Pu was undermined by Duosun, who repeatedly reported his shortcomings to the throne; when the emperor asked Fang, he answered, "My office is to draft edicts; I do not know what Pu has done. " Before long Pu was sent out to govern a military circuit, and Duosun was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
4
雍熙元年郊祀，命昉與琪並為左右僕射，昉固辭，乃加中書侍郎。 王師討幽薊不利，遣使分詣河南、東，籍民為兵，凡八丁取一。 昉等相率奏曰：「近者分遣使籍河南、東四十餘郡之民以為邊備，非得已也。 然河南之民素習農桑，罔知戰鬥，一旦括集，必致動搖，若因而嘯聚，更須剪除。 如此，則河北閭閻既困於戎馬，河南生聚復擾於萑蒲，矧當春和，有妨農作。 陛下若以明詔既頒，難於反汗，則當續遣使臣，嚴加戒飭，所至點募，人情若有不安，即須少緩，密奏取裁，庶免後患。 」上嘉納之。
At the Yongxi suburban sacrifice, Fang and Qi were both named Left and Right Vice Directors, but Fang firmly declined and was made Vice Director of the Secretariat instead. The campaign against You and Ji faltered; the court sent envoys to Henan and the eastern circuits to register civilians for military service, drafting one man from every eight households. Fang and his colleagues jointly submitted: "Envoys have lately been sent to register the people of more than forty prefectures in Henan and the east for frontier defense—this was not undertaken lightly. Yet the people of Henan have long lived by farming and sericulture and know nothing of war; once they are conscripted en masse, unrest is inevitable, and if they rise in bands, the court will have to suppress them again. In that case the hamlets of Hebei will already be exhausted by war, and the households of Henan will again be ravaged by rebellion; besides, spring is here, and the farming season must not be disrupted. If Your Majesty feels bound by a decree already promulgated, then send further envoys with stern orders: wherever conscription proceeds, if the people show any sign of unrest, slow the levy at once and report secretly for the throne's decision, so that later troubles may be averted. The emperor approved the memorial and acted on it.
5
端拱初，布衣翟馬周擊登聞鼓，訟昉居宰相位，當北方有事之時，不為邊備，徒知賦詩宴樂。 屬耤田禮方畢，乃詔學士賈黃中草制，罷昉為右僕射，且加切責。 黃中言：「僕射，百僚師長，實宰相之任，今自工部尚書而遷是職，非黜責也。 若曰文昌務簡，以均勞逸為辭，斯為得體。 」上然之。 會邊警益急，詔文武群臣各進策備禦，昉又引漢、唐故事，深以屈己修好、弭兵息民為言，時論稱之。
Early in the Duan Gong era, a commoner named Zhai Mazhou struck the petition drum, charging that while Fang sat as chief minister and the north was in crisis, he made no preparations for the frontier but only wrote poetry and gave banquets. Just as the plowing ceremony had concluded, the emperor ordered Academician Jia Huangzhong to draft an edict demoting Fang to Right Vice Director with a sharp reprimand. Huangzhong said, "The Vice Director is the senior of all officials and in substance holds the chief minister's role; promotion from Minister of Works to this office is not a punishment. If the edict speaks of easing duties at the Secretariat and sharing the burden for the sake of repose, that would be fitting. The emperor accepted his view. As frontier alarms intensified, the court ordered civil and military officials to submit plans for defense; Fang again drew on Han and Tang precedents, urging the emperor to humble himself in seeking peace, halt the fighting, and let the people rest—an argument widely praised.
6
淳化二年，復以本官兼中書侍郎、平章事，監修國史。 三年夏，旱蝗，既雨。 時昉與張齊賢、賈黃中、李沆同居宰輔，以燮理非材，上表待罪，上不之罪。 四年，昉以私門連遭憂戚，求解機務，詔不允，遣齊賢等諭旨，復起視事。 後數月，罷為右僕射。 先是，上召張洎草制，授昉左僕射，罷相，洎言：「昉居燮理之任，而陰陽乖戾，不能決意引退，俾居百僚師長之任，何以示勸？ 」上覽奏，乃令罷守本官。
In the second year of Chunhua he was again made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor while retaining his former rank, with charge of compiling the national history. In the summer of the third year drought and locusts struck; rain followed. Fang then shared the chief ministry with Zhang Qixian, Jia Huangzhong, and Li Hang; judging themselves unequal to the task of governing, they submitted memorials asking to be punished, but the emperor declined to reproach them. In the fourth year, with his family struck by repeated mourning, Fang asked to be relieved of high office; the emperor refused, sent Qixian and others to explain his wishes, and Fang returned to duty. A few months later he was demoted to Right Vice Director. Earlier the emperor had Zhang Ji draft an edict making Fang Left Vice Director and removing him from the chief ministry; Ji argued, "Fang held the task of governing the realm, yet heaven and earth were out of harmony and he would not step down; to set him in the post that heads all officials—what lesson does that teach? After reading Ji's memorial, the emperor ordered Fang dismissed from the chief ministry but left in his former rank.
7
晉侍中崧者，與昉同宗且同里，時人謂崧為東李家，昉為西李家。 漢末，崧被誅。 至是，其子璨自蘇州常熟縣令赴調，昉為訟其父冤，且言：「周太祖已為昭雪贈官，還其田宅，錄璨而官之。 然璨年幾五十，尚淹州縣之職，臣昔與之同難，豈宜叨遇聖明。 儻推一視之仁，澤及衰微之祚，則已往之冤獲伸於下，而繼絕之恩永光簡冊矣。 」詔授璨著作佐郎，後官至右讚善大夫。
The Jin Vice Director Song was Fang's clansman and fellow townsman; contemporaries called Song's branch the eastern Li family and Fang's the western Li family. At the end of Later Han, Song was put to death. Now his son Can arrived from his post as magistrate of Changshu in Suzhou to seek a new appointment; Fang petitioned to redress his father's wrong, adding, "Emperor Taizu of Zhou had already posthumously rehabilitated him, granted him office, restored his lands and house, and given Can an appointment. Yet Can is nearly fifty and still stuck in county and prefectural posts; I once shared his family's ruin—how should he presume on Your Majesty's grace? If Your Majesty extends equal mercy to the fallen and favors a house in decline, then old wrongs will be righted in this life and the grace of continuing a cut-off line will shine forever in the records. The throne appointed Can Assistant Compiler; he later rose to Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
8
二年，陪祀南郊，禮畢入賀，因拜舞仆地，臺吏掖之以出，臥疾數日薨，年七十二。 贈司徒，諡文正。
In the second year, while attending the suburban sacrifice, he entered to offer congratulations after the rites, bowed, and collapsed; censorate clerks helped him out; he lay ill for several days and died at seventy-two. He was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor with the temple name Wenzheng.
9
昉和厚多恕，不念舊惡，在位小心循謹，無赫赫稱。 為文章慕白居易，尤淺近易曉。 好接賓客，江南平，士大夫歸朝者多從之遊。 雅厚張洎而薄張佖，及昉罷相，洎草制深攻詆之，而佖朔望必詣昉。 或謂佖曰：「李公待君素不厚，何數詣之？ 」佖曰：「我為廷尉日，李公方秉政，未嘗一有請求，此吾所以重之也。」
Fang was gentle and magnanimous, slow to remember injuries; in office he was cautious and meticulous, without showy reputation. As a writer he took Bai Juyi as his model, favoring language plain and readily understood. He delighted in entertaining guests; after the conquest of the south, many southern scholars newly arrived at court sought his company. He held Zhang Ji in high regard but thought little of Zhang Yi; when Fang left office, Ji drafted the edict and vilified him bitterly, yet Yi still visited Fang on every first and fifteenth of the month. Someone asked Yi, "Lord Li has never favored you—why do you call on him so often? Yi replied, "When I was Commandant of Justice and Lord Li was in power, he never once asked a favor of me—that is why I hold him in esteem."
10
昉所居有園亭別墅之勝，多召故人親友宴樂其中。 既致政，欲尋洛中九老故事，時吏部尚書宋琪年七十九，左諫議大夫楊徽之年七十五，郢州刺史魏丕年七十六，太常少卿致仕李運年八十，水部郎中朱昂年七十一，廬州節度副使武允成年七十九，太子中允致仕張好問年八十五，吳僧讚寧年七十八，議將集，會蜀寇而罷。
His home boasted gardens, pavilions, and country villas; he often gathered old friends and relatives there for feasting and pleasure. After retirement he hoped to revive the tradition of the Nine Old Men of Luoyang: Minister of Personnel Song Qi was seventy-nine, Left Remonstrator Yang Weizhi seventy-five, Prefect of Ying Wei Pi seventy-six, retired Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Yun eighty, Director in the Ministry of Water Zhu Ang seventy-one, Military Vice Commissioner of Luzhou Wu Yongnian seventy-nine, retired Crown Prince's Attendant Zhang Haowen eighty-five, and the Wu monk Zanning seventy-eight—they meant to gather, but unrest in Shu forced them to abandon the plan.
11
昉素與盧多遜善，待之不疑，多遜屢譖昉於上，或以告昉，不之信。 及入相，太宗言及多遜事，昉頗為解釋。 帝曰：「多遜居常毀卿一錢不直。 」昉始信之。 上由此益重昉。
Fang had long been close to Lu Duosun and trusted him without reserve; Duosun repeatedly slandered Fang to the throne, and though others warned him, Fang refused to believe it. After he became chief minister, Emperor Taizong spoke of Duosun's actions, and Fang offered a spirited defense. The emperor said, "Duosun routinely says you are not worth a single coin. Only then did Fang believe the reports. From this the emperor valued Fang still more highly.
12
昉居中書日，有求進用者，雖知其材可取，必正色拒絕之，已而擢用； 或不足用，必和顏溫語待之。 子弟問其故，曰：「用賢，人主之事； 若受其請，是市私恩也，故峻絕之，使恩歸於上。 若不用者，既失所望，又無善辭，取怨之道也。」
While Fang sat in the Secretariat, those who sought promotion—even when he knew their talent merited use—were met with a stern refusal; yet afterward he would advance them. Those unfit for appointment he received with a kindly manner and gentle speech. When his sons and nephews asked why, he said, "Putting the worthy in office is the ruler's business. To accept their pleas is to trade in private favor; so I refuse them harshly and let the credit belong to the throne. If they are not appointed, they have lost their hope and receive no gracious reply—that is how resentment is bred."
13
初，超未有子，昉母謝方娠，指腹謂伯母張曰：「生男當與伯母為子。 」故昉出繼於超。 昉再相，因表其事，求贈所生父母官。 詔贈其祖溫太子太傅，祖母權氏莒國太夫人，起太子太師，謝氏鄭國太夫人。
Earlier, before Chao had a son, Fang's mother Xie was pregnant; she pointed at her belly and told her sister-in-law Zhang, "If I bear a son, he shall be your son. Thus Fang was adopted as Chao's heir. When Fang served as chief minister again, he submitted a memorial on the matter and asked that offices be granted his biological parents. The throne posthumously honored his grandfather Wen as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, his grandmother Lady Quan as Lady of the State of Ju, his father Qi as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and his mother Lady Xie as Lady of the State of Zheng.
14
昉素病心悸，數歲一發，發必彌年而後愈，蓋典誥命三十餘年，勞役思慮所致。 及居相位，益加憂畏。 有文集五十卷。 子四人：宗訥、宗誨、宗諤、宗諒。 宗誨，右讚善大夫。 宗諒，主賓客員外郎。
Fang had long suffered heart palpitations; every few years they recurred, and each attack lasted nearly a year before he recovered—likely the toll of drafting edicts for more than thirty years. Once he held the chief ministry, his anxiety only grew. His collected writings ran to fifty juan. He had four sons: Zongne, Zonghui, Zong'e, and Zongliang. Zonghui served as Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent. Zongliang was Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions.
15
子宗訥
His son Zongne
16
宗訥，字大辨，以蔭補太廟齋郎，遷第四室長。 代謁吏部銓，邊光範意其年少，未能屬辭，語之曰：「苟援筆成六韻詩，雖不試書判，可入等矣。 」宗訥易之，光範試詩賦，立就。 明日，遂擬授秘書省正字； 又明日，上命擢國子監丞。 蓋上居藩邸時，每有篇詠，令昉屬和，前後數百章，皆宗訥繕寫，上愛其楷麗，問知為宗訥所書，故有是命。 太平興國初，詔賈黃中集《神醫普救方》，宗訥暨劉錫、吳淑、呂文仲、杜鎬、舒雅皆預焉。 雍熙初，昉在相位，上欲命宗訥為尚書郎，昉懇辭，以為非承平故事，止改秘書丞，歷太常博士。
Zongne, styled Dabian, entered service through yin privilege as Aide of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was promoted to chief of the fourth shrine. When he stood in for his father at the Ministry's selection board, Bian Guangfan thought him too young to draft documents and said, "If you can write a regulated verse in six rhymes on the spot, you may pass the grade even without the document test. Zongne agreed; Guangfan tested him in poetry and fu, and he completed them immediately. The next day he was provisionally named Proofreader of the Secretariat; the day after that the emperor ordered him promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education. While the emperor still lived in the princely residence, each time he composed a poem he had Fang write a matching verse; several hundred such pieces were all transcribed by Zongne; the emperor admired the elegant regular script, learned Zongne had written them, and therefore issued this command. At the start of Taiping Xingguo the court ordered Jia Huangzhong to compile the Comprehensive Relief Formulas of the Divine Physician; Zongne joined Liu Xi, Wu Shu, Lü Wenzhong, Du Hao, and Shu Ya in the work. Early in Yongxi, while Fang was chief minister, the emperor wished to make Zongne a Secretariat Director; Fang firmly declined, arguing it was not custom in settled times, and Zongne remained Secretariat Vice Director, later serving as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
17
宗訥頗習典禮。 淳化中，呂端掌禮院，引宗訥同判，累遷比部郎中。 咸平六年，卒，年五十五。 子昭迴，大中祥符五年獻文，召試賜進士第，後為屯田員外郎。 昭遜，太子中舍。
Zongne was well versed in ritual protocol. During Chunhua, Lü Duan headed the Ritual Institute and brought Zongne in as associate director; Zongne rose step by step to Director in the Ministry of Revenue. In the sixth year of Xianping he died at fifty-five. His son Zhaohui, in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, submitted a literary work, was examined at court and given the jinshi degree, and later served as Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms. Zhaoxun was Attendant of the Crown Prince.
18
子宗諤
His son Zong'e
19
宗諤，字昌武，七歲能屬文，恥以父蔭得官，獨由鄉舉，第進士，授校書郎。 明年，獻文自薦，遷秘書郎、集賢校理、同修起居注。 先是，後苑陪宴，校理官不與，京官乘馬不得入禁門。 至是，皆因宗諤之請復之，遂為故事。
Zong'e, styled Changwu, could write prose at seven; ashamed to take office through his father's privilege, he entered service only by the provincial examinations, passed as jinshi, and was made Proofreader. The following year he submitted a self-recommended literary work and was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose. Previously, at banquets in the rear park, collators were not invited, and capital officials on horseback were barred from the inner gate. Now both privileges were restored at Zong'e's petition and thereafter became fixed practice.
20
真宗即位，拜起居舍人，預重修《太祖實錄》。 從幸大名，上疏曰：「國家馭邊之術，制勝之謀，將帥之短長，兵衛之眾寡，宸算廟謨，盡在吾術中矣。 今之言事者，不過請陛下益兵貯糧，分道掩殺，言之甚易，行之則難。 始受命則無不以攻堅陷陣為壯圖，及遇敵則惟以閉壘塞關為上計，孤君父之重委，致生靈之重困，興言及此，誠可歎息。 自古行軍出師，無不首擇將帥。 夫將帥隨材任使，守一郡，控一城，分領驍勇，爭據要害，又豈直三路主帥之名，然後能制六師生死之命乎？ 今陛下選任非不至也，權位非不重也，告戒非不丁寧也，處置非不專一也； 而外敵犯塞，車駕親征，曾不聞出一人一騎為之救助，不知深溝高壘，秣馬厲兵，欲安用哉？ 臣以為臨軍易帥，拔卒為將，在此時也。 有功者拔於朝，不用者戮於市，亦此時也。 惟陛下圖之。 然後下哀痛之詔，行蠲復之恩。 回鸞上都，垂衣當寧，豈不盛哉。」
When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Zong'e was made Drafter of Activity and Repose and helped revise the Veritable Records of Taizu. On the journey to Daming he submitted a memorial: "The state's frontier policy, its plans for victory, the strengths and weaknesses of its commanders, and the size of the guard—the court's calculations and secret strategies are all set down in our books. Today's advisers do nothing but urge Your Majesty to raise more troops, stock more grain, and send columns to raid and kill—the words are easy; the deeds are hard. At first every commander vows to storm walls and break lines; yet when the enemy appears the highest wisdom is to shut the passes and bar the gates, betraying the heavy trust of ruler and father and plunging the people into misery—at the thought one can only sigh. Since antiquity no army has marched without first choosing its commanders. Commanders should be matched to their gifts—holding one district, defending one walled city, leading the bold to seize vital ground—need they bear only the title of commander of the three routes before they can hold the fate of the Six Armies in their hands? Today Your Majesty's appointments are not wanting, their powers not slight, your warnings not lacking in earnestness, your orders not lacking in focus; yet when enemies cross the border and the emperor campaigns in person, not a single rider is sent to their relief; if deep moats, high walls, fed horses, and honed blades serve no purpose, what are they for? I believe that replacing commanders on the eve of battle and promoting soldiers to generalship is what the moment demands. Reward the successful at court; execute the useless in the marketplace—that too is for this moment. Only Your Majesty can decide. Then issue an edict of compassion and grant tax remissions. Return the imperial procession to the capital and rule at ease from the throne—would that not be magnificent?"

In the second year of Jingde he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy. That autumn, as the suburban sacrifice approached, he was ordered to oversee the Great Music Office and the Office of Drum and Pipe Music. Previously musicians were promoted chiefly by seniority, until some clutched their instruments yet knew nothing of music. Zong'e had long understood pitch and mode; he added scrutiny and memorialized to dismiss fifty unqualified performers. He restored the instruments, revised office titles, and submitted twenty recommendations for reform; the emperor read them and expressed his admiration. The full account appears in the Treatise on Music. He also wrote a Music Compendium and presented it; the court ordered it filed in the Historiography Institute, and thereafter rehearsals were held twice monthly.

Zong'e was on the verge of high appointment when his early death cut him off—a loss the court deeply regretted. 初，昉居三館、兩制之職，宗諤不數年，皆踐其地。 風流儒雅，藏書萬卷。 內行淳至，事繼母符氏以孝聞。 二兄早世，奉嫂字孤，恩禮兼盡。 與弟宗諒友愛尤至，覃恩所及，必先群從，及歿而己子有未仕者。 程宿早卒，有弟無所依，宗諤為表請於朝而官之。 勤接士類，無賢不肖，恂恂盡禮，獎拔後進，唯恐不及，以是士人皆歸仰之。
Fang had held every post in the Three Institutes and the two drafting offices; Zong'e within a few years had filled them all. Elegant in bearing, he kept a library of ten thousand juan. In private life he was utterly sincere; his devotion to his stepmother Lady Fu won renown for filial piety. Both his elder brothers died young; he cared for his sister-in-law and raised her orphaned children, showing every measure of kindness and propriety. His bond with his younger brother Zongliang was especially close; whenever imperial favor reached the clan, he always gave his collaterals priority first, and at his death some of his own sons had still not received appointments. Cheng Su died young, leaving a younger brother with no one to depend on; Zong'e submitted a memorial to the court and secured an appointment for him. He welcomed scholars tirelessly, treating the worthy and unworthy alike with steady courtesy, promoting younger men whenever he could and fearing he had not done enough; for this scholars everywhere looked up to him.

Zong'e excelled at clerical script. He left a collected works in sixty juan and Inner and Outer Drafts in thirty juan. He helped compile the Continued Tongdian, the Record of the Dazhong xiangfu Feng and Fen sacrifices, and route gazetteers for the provinces, and also wrote Family Traditions and Collected Conversations, all of which circulated widely. His sons were Zhaoyao, Zhaoshu, and Zhaoshi.

Grandson: Zhaoshu

昭述，字仲祖，以父蔭為秘書省校書郎。 召試學士院，賜進士出身，為刑部詳覆官，累遷秘書丞。 群牧制置使曹利用薦為判官，鄆州牧地侵於民者凡數千頃，昭述悉復之。 以太常博士知開封縣，特遷尚書屯田員外郎、開封推官。 坐嘗被曹利用薦，出知常州，遷為三司度支判官，改河北轉運使。 江陵屯兵讙言倉粟陳腐，欲以動眾。 昭述取以為奉，且以飯其僚屬，眾遂定。
Zhaoshu, styled Zhongzu, entered office through his father's privilege as a proofreader in the Secretariat. Called to examination at the Hanlin Academy, he was granted jinshi standing, served as a detailed-review officer in the Ministry of Justice, and rose to Secretariat aide. Cao Liyong, commissioner for herds, recommended him as an administrative aide; in Yanzhou thousands of qing of pastureland had been taken from commoners, and Zhaoshu restored all of it. As an erudite of the Grand Secretariat he governed Kaifeng County, then was specially promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's farms bureau and investigating commissioner for Kaifeng. Because he had once been recommended by Cao Liyong, he was posted out to govern Changzhou, then became a fiscal administrative aide in the Three Departments and was transferred to Hebei transport commissioner. At Jiangling the garrison troops spread word that the granary grain was stale and rotten, hoping to stir up a mutiny. Zhaoshu took the grain for his own table and fed his staff from it as well, and the troops quieted down.

When Liu Liufu first passed through, he took it for a dike repair; on his return the fortress stood complete, and he was deeply astonished. When the volunteer militia was first established, public unrest ran high; Zhaoshu rode post relays several stages a day, explained the policy to local elders, and the people calmed down. Lü Mengzheng

呂蒙正，字聖功，河南人。 祖夢奇，戶部侍郎。 父龜圖，起居郎。 蒙正，太平興國二年，擢進士第一，授將作監丞，通判昇州。 陛辭，有旨，民事有不便者，許騎置以聞，賜錢二十萬。 代還，會征太原，召見行在，授著作郎、直史館，加左拾遺。 五年，親拜左補闕、知制誥。
Lü Mengzheng, whose courtesy name was Shenggong, came from Henan. His grandfather Mengqi had been vice minister of the household bureau. His father Qitu had been an attendant gentleman. In the second year of Taiping xingguo, Mengzheng took first place among the jinshi, was appointed an aide in the Directorate of Works, and made vice commissioner of Sheng Prefecture. At his farewell audience he was told that wherever civil affairs proved inconvenient he might use post relays to report it, and he was granted two hundred thousand in cash. On returning from his post during the Taiyuan campaign, he was summoned to the emperor's camp, made a compiler and drafter of the Historiography Institute, and given the added title of left remonstrance. In the fifth year he was personally appointed left supplementation censor and document drafter.

初，龜圖多內寵，與妻劉氏不睦，並蒙正出之，頗淪躓窘乏，劉誓不復嫁。 及蒙正登仕，迎二親，同堂異室，奉養備至。 龜圖旋卒，詔起復。 未幾，遷都官郎中，入為翰林學士，擢左諫議大夫、參知政事，賜第麗景門。 上謂之曰：「凡士未達，見當世之務戾於理者，則怏怏於心； 及列於位，得以獻可替否，當盡其所蘊，雖言未必盡中，亦當僉議而更之，俾協於道。 朕固不以崇高自恃，使人不敢言也。 」蒙正初入朝堂，有朝士指之曰：「此子亦參政耶？ 」蒙正陽為不聞而過之，同列不能平，詰其姓名，蒙正遽止之曰：「若一知其姓名，則終身不能忘，不若毋知之為愈也。 」時皆服其量。
At first Qitu had kept many concubines and quarreled with his wife Lady Liu; both cast Mengzheng out, and he knew poverty and hardship; Liu swore never to remarry. Once Mengzheng rose in office he welcomed both parents home; they shared one hall in separate chambers, and he supported them with every care. Qitu soon died; the throne ordered him to resume office without completing mourning. Before long he became director of the Ministry of Personnel, entered the Hanlin Academy, was promoted to left remonstrance grand master and vice councilor, and was given a mansion at Lijing Gate. The emperor told him, "Before a gentleman has risen, he broods over every affair of the age that runs against reason; Once in office he should offer what is sound and reject what is not, and bring forth all he has stored; even if his words do not all strike true, the court should debate and amend them until they accord with the Way. I certainly do not stand on my eminence and silence those who would speak." When Mengzheng first entered the court hall, a court gentleman pointed at him and said, "This fellow is a councilor too? Mengzheng feigned not to hear and walked on; his colleagues could not contain themselves and demanded the man's name; Mengzheng quickly stopped them and said, "Once you know a man's name you never forget it for life; better never to know at all." All present admired his forbearance.
45
李昉罷相，蒙正拜中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事，監修國史。 蒙正質厚寬簡，有重望，以正道自持。 遇事敢言，每論時政，有未允者，必固稱不可，上嘉其無隱。 趙普開國元老，蒙正後進，歷官一紀，遂同相位，普甚推許之。 俄丁內艱，起復。
When Li Fang left the chief councilorship, Mengzheng was made vice director of the Secretariat, concurrent minister of revenue, and chief councilor, with charge of the national history. Mengzheng was plain, steady, and broad-minded, commanded deep respect, and held himself to the upright path. He spoke boldly whenever affairs arose; in every discussion of policy, if something seemed wrong he firmly said it could not stand, and the emperor praised his candor. Zhao Pu was a founding elder of the dynasty; Mengzheng came later, yet after a full cycle of offices they shared the chief councilorship, and Pu greatly esteemed him. He soon mourned his mother; the throne granted leave from mourning.
46
先是，盧多遜為相，其子雍起家即授水部員外郎，後遂以為常。 至是，蒙正奏曰：「臣忝甲科及第，釋褐止授九品京官。 況天下才能，老於巖穴，不霑寸祿者多矣。 今臣男始離襁褓，膺此寵命，恐罹陰譴，乞以臣釋褐時官補之。 」自是宰相子止授九品京官，遂為定制。
Earlier, when Lu Duosun was chief councilor, his son Yong upon entering office had immediately been made vice director of the water bureau, and that had since become custom. Mengzheng now memorialized, "Your servant took first place in the jinshi examination; upon leaving student robes I received only a ninth-rank capital post. Moreover, throughout the realm men of talent who have grown old in reclusion without a scrap of salary are countless. Now my son has just left the swaddling clothes and receives this favored appointment; I fear hidden reproach and beg that he receive the post I held when I first left student robes." Thereafter chief councilors' sons received only ninth-rank capital posts, and the rule became permanent.
47
朝士有藏古鏡者，自言能照二百里，欲獻之蒙正以求知。 蒙正笑曰：「吾面不過楪子大，安用照二百里哉？ 」聞者歎服。
A court gentleman owned an antique mirror and claimed it could see two hundred li, hoping to present it to Mengzheng and win his notice. Mengzheng laughed and said, "My face is no larger than a dinner plate—what need have I to see two hundred li? Those who heard it sighed in admiration.
48
淳化中，左正言宋沆上疏忤旨，沆，蒙正妻族，坐是罷為吏部尚書，復相李昉。 四年，昉罷，蒙正復以本官入相。 因對，論及征伐，上曰：「朕比來征討，蓋為民除暴，苟好功黷武，則天下之人熸亡盡矣。 」蒙正對曰：「隋、唐數十年中，四征遼碣，人不堪命。 煬帝全軍陷沒，太宗自運土木攻城，如此卒無所濟。 且治國之要，在內修政事，則遠人來歸，自致安靜。 」上韙之。
In the Chunhua era left rectifier Song Hang submitted a memorial that offended the emperor; Hang was kin to Mengzheng's wife, and for this Mengzheng was dismissed as minister of personnel while Li Fang was again made chief councilor. In the fourth year Fang left office and Mengzheng again entered as chief councilor under his former title. In audience they discussed warfare; the emperor said, "My recent campaigns have been to rid the people of tyranny; if one loves achievement and abuses arms, the people of the realm will perish to the last man." Mengzheng replied, "Across several decades Sui and Tang campaigned four times against Liaodong, and the people could not endure the burden. Emperor Yang lost his entire army; Emperor Taizong himself hauled earth and timber to besiege cities—yet in the end nothing was gained. The essentials of governing a state lie in strengthening government at home; then distant peoples come of themselves and peace follows without force. The emperor approved his words.
49
嘗燈夕設宴，蒙正侍，上語之曰：「五代之際，生靈凋喪，周太祖自鄴南歸，士庶皆罹剽掠，下則火災，上則彗孛，觀者恐懼，當時謂無復太平之日矣。 朕躬覽庶政，萬事粗理，每念上天之貺，致此繁盛，乃知理亂在人。 」蒙正避席曰：「乘輿所在，士庶走集，故繁盛如此。 臣嘗見都城外不數里，饑寒而死者甚眾，不必盡然。 願陛下視近以及遠，蒼生之幸也。 」上變色不言。 蒙正侃然復位，同列多其直諒。
Once at a Lantern Festival banquet Mengzheng attended, the emperor told him, "In the Five Dynasties the people were wasted away; when Zhou Taizu returned south from Ye, scholars and commoners alike were plundered; fires raged below and comets above; onlookers trembled, and many said peace would never return. I myself oversee the myriad affairs and all is roughly in order; whenever I reflect on Heaven's gift that has brought this flourishing age, I know that order and disorder lie in men. Mengzheng rose from his mat and said, "Where the imperial carriage stands, scholars and commoners gather, and so the capital looks flourishing. I have seen, not many li beyond the capital wall, the hungry and cold dying in great numbers; it is not all as you say. I beg Your Majesty to look from what is near to what is far—that is the fortune of the common people. The emperor's face changed and he fell silent. Mengzheng calmly resumed his seat; his colleagues admired his blunt honesty.
50
上嘗欲遣人使朔方，諭中書選才而可責以事者，蒙正退以名上，上不許。 他日，三問，三以其人對。 上曰：「卿何執耶？ 」蒙正曰：「臣非執，蓋陛下未諒爾。 」固稱：「其人可使，餘人不及。 臣不欲用媚道妄隨人主意，以害國事。 」同列悚息不敢動。 上退謂左右曰：「蒙正氣量，我不如。 」既而卒用蒙正所薦，果稱職。
The emperor once wished to send an envoy to Shuo Prefecture and told the Secretariat to choose someone capable of bearing responsibility; Mengzheng withdrew and submitted a name; the emperor refused. On another day he asked three times; three times Mengzheng named the same man. The emperor said, "Why are you so stubborn? Mengzheng said, "I am not stubborn—Your Majesty simply has not yet understood. He insisted, "This man can be sent; no one else equals him. I do not wish to use flattery and follow others' whims at the cost of state affairs. His colleagues held their breath and dared not stir. The emperor withdrew and told his attendants, "Mengzheng's magnanimity—I am not his equal. He soon used the man Mengzheng had recommended, who indeed proved competent.
51
至道初，以右僕射出判河南府兼西京留守。 蒙正至洛，多引親舊歡宴，政尚寬靜，委任僚屬，事多總裁而已。
At the beginning of Zhidao he was made right vice director of the Secretariat and sent out to judge Henan Prefecture, concurrently regent of the Western Capital. At Luoyang he often gathered kin and old friends for feasts; his government favored leniency and ease; he entrusted affairs to subordinates and reserved final decisions to himself.
52
真宗即位，進左僕射。 會營奉熙陵，蒙正追感先朝不次之遇，奉家財三百餘萬以助用。 葬日，伏哭盡哀，人以為得大臣體。 咸平四年，以本官同平章事、昭文館大學士。 國朝以來三入相者，惟趙普與蒙正焉。 郊祀禮成，加司空兼門下侍郎。 六年，授太子太師，封萊國公，改封徐，又封許。
When Zhenzong succeeded the throne, Mengzheng was promoted to left vice director of the Secretariat. When the Yongxi Mausoleum was being built, moved by the former court's extraordinary favor, he presented more than three million from his family wealth to help fund the work. On the burial day he prostrated himself and wept until spent; observers said he had shown a great minister's bearing. In the fourth year of Xianping he was again made chief councilor under his former title and grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall. Since the founding of the dynasty only Zhao Pu and Mengzheng had thrice entered the chief councilorship. When the suburban sacrifice was completed, he was given concurrent minister of works and vice director of the Department of State. In the sixth year he was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent, enfeoffed as Duke of Lai, then given the Xu fief, and finally enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
53
景德二年春，表請歸洛。 陛辭日，肩輿至東園門，命二子掖以升殿，因言：「遠人請和，弭兵省財，古今上策，惟願陛下以百姓為念。 」上嘉納之，因遷從簡太子洗馬，知簡奉禮郎。 蒙正至洛，有園亭花木，日與親舊宴會，子孫環列，迭奉壽觴，怡然自得。 大中祥符而後，上朝永熙陵，封泰山，祠后土，過洛，兩幸其第，錫賚有加。 上謂蒙正曰：「卿諸子孰可用？ 」對曰：「諸子皆不足用。 有侄夷簡，任潁州推官，宰相才也。 」夷簡由是見知於上。
In the spring of the second year of Jingde he memorialized asking to retire to Luoyang. On the day of his farewell audience he was carried in a sedan to the Eastern Garden Gate and had his two sons help him up the hall, saying, "The distant peoples seek peace; to still arms and save wealth is the supreme strategy of every age—I only beg Your Majesty to keep the common people in mind. The emperor praised and accepted this; he therefore promoted Congjian to crown prince study companion and Zhi to court gentleman for offering. At Luoyang he had gardens, pavilions, flowers, and trees; day after day he feasted with kin and old friends while sons and grandsons ranged about him, passing cups in turn, content and at ease. After Dazhong xiangfu he attended court at the Yongxi Mausoleum, performed the Feng and Fen sacrifices, and passed through Luoyang; twice the emperor visited his home and heaped gifts upon him. The emperor asked Mengzheng, "Which of your sons can be put to use? He replied, "None of my sons is adequate. I have a nephew Yijian, investigating commissioner in Yingzhou—he has the talent of a chief councilor. Yijian thereby came to the emperor's notice.
54
富言者，蒙正客也。 一日白曰：「兒子十許歲，欲令入書院，事廷評、太祝。 」蒙正許之。 及見，驚曰：「此兒他日名位與吾相似，而勳業遠過於吾。 」令與諸子同學，供給甚厚。 言之子，即弼也。 後弼兩入相，亦以司徒致仕。 其知人類如此。
Fu Yan was Mengzheng's guest. One day he reported, "My son of about ten years wishes to enter the academy to study for the posts of reviewing censor and court gentleman for offering. Mengzheng agreed. When he saw the boy he was startled and said, "This boy's later name and rank will resemble mine, yet his achievements will far surpass mine. He had him study with his sons and supplied him generously. Yan's son was none other than Bi. Later Bi twice entered the chief councilorship and likewise retired as minister of works. His judgment of men was of this sort.
55
許國之命甫下而卒，年六十八。 贈中書令，諡曰文穆。
The order enfeoffing him as Duke of Xu had just been issued when he died, aged sixty-eight. He was posthumously made vice director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous title Wenmu.
56
蒙正初為相時，張紳知蔡州，坐贓免。 或言於上曰：「紳家富，不至此，特蒙正貧時勾索不如意，今報之爾。 」上命即復紳官，蒙正不辯。 後考課院得紳實狀，復黜為絳州團練副使。 及蒙正再入相，太宗謂曰：「張紳果有贓。 」蒙正不辯亦不謝。 在西京日，上數遣中貴人將命至，蒙正待之如在相位時，不少貶，時人重焉。
When Mengzheng first became chief councilor, Zhang Shen governed Caizhou and was dismissed for corruption. Someone told the emperor, "Shen's family is wealthy and would not stoop to this—it is only that when Mengzheng was poor, Shen pressed him harshly, and now he repays the old score. The emperor at once restored Shen to office; Mengzheng did not argue. Later the Performance Review Bureau obtained Shen's true circumstances and again demoted him to military training vice commissioner of Jiangzhou. When Mengzheng again entered as chief councilor, Taizong said, "Zhang Shen truly was corrupt." Mengzheng neither argued nor thanked. During his years in the Western Capital the emperor several times sent palace eunuchs with orders; Mengzheng received them with the same ceremony as when he had held the chief councilorship, not diminishing himself in the least, and men of the time respected him for it.
57
子從簡，再為國子博士； 惟簡，太子中舍； 承簡，司門員外郎； 行簡，比部員外郎； 務簡，亦國子博士； 居簡，殿中丞； 知簡，太子右讚善大夫。 蒙正弟蒙休，咸平進士，至殿中丞。
His son Cong Jian again served as Director of Studies at the Imperial Academy; Wei Jian served as Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household; Cheng Jian was Vice Director of the Gate Office; Xing Jian was Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; Wu Jian also served as Director of Studies at the Imperial Academy; Ju Jian was Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat; Zhi Jian was Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent for Good Conduct. Mengzheng's younger brother Meng Xiu, a Xianping advanced scholar, rose to Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat.
58
龜圖弟龜祥，殿中丞、知壽州。 子蒙亨，舉進士高等，既廷試，以蒙正居中書，故報罷。 後歷下蔡、武平主簿。 至道初，考課州縣官，蒙亨引對，文學、政事俱優，命為光祿寺丞，改大理寺丞，卒。 次子蒙巽，虞部員外郎； 蒙周，淳化進士及第。 蒙亨子即夷簡也。 次子宗簡，亦進士及第。
Gui Tu's younger brother Gui Xiang served as Assistant Director of the Palace Secretariat and prefect of Shou Prefecture. His son Meng Heng ranked high in the metropolitan examination, but after the palace examination his result was voided because Mengzheng held the Central Secretariat. He later served as registrar of Xia Cai and Wuping. At the beginning of the Zhidao era, when prefectural and county officials were evaluated, Meng Heng was presented at court. His literary and administrative merits were both excellent. He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and died. His second son Meng Xi was Vice Director of the Ministry of Works; Meng Zhou was a Chunhua advanced scholar. Meng Heng's son was none other than Yijian. His second son Zong Jian also passed the advanced examination.
59
慶曆中，居簡提點京東刑獄，時夏竦有憾於石介，介死，竦言於上曰：「介未嘗死，北走鄰國矣。 」乃遣中使發棺驗之。 居簡謂曰：「萬一介果死，則朝廷為無故發人之墓，奈何？ 」中使曰：「於君何如？ 」居簡曰：「介死，當時必有內外親族及門生會葬，問之可也。 」中使乃令結狀保證以聞，介事乃白。 居簡長者，其行事多類此。
During the Qingli era, Ju Jian served as judicial intendant of the Jingdong Circuit. At that time Xia Song bore a grudge against Shi Jie. After Jie died, Song told the emperor, "Jie did not in fact die; he has fled north to a neighboring state. " The court then sent a palace envoy to open the coffin and verify. Ju Jian said to him, "If Jie truly is dead, the court will have opened a man's tomb without cause. What then? " The envoy said, "What is that to you? " Ju Jian said, "If Jie is dead, kinsmen and students must have attended the burial at the time. They can be questioned. " The envoy then required written guarantees before reporting, and the matter of Jie was clarified. Ju Jian was a man of mature judgment, and much of his conduct was of this kind.
60
徐州妖人孔直溫挾左道誘軍士為變，或詣轉運使告，不受詞。 居簡令易其牒，盡捕究黨與，貸詿誤者，請於朝，斬直溫等。 濮州復叛，都民驚潰，居簡馳往，獲首惡誅之。 因大閱兵享勞，姦不得發。 用二事，遷秩鹽鐵判官，拜集賢院學士、知梓州、應天府，徙荊南，進龍圖閣直學士、知廣州，陶甓甃城，人以為便。 以兵部侍郎判西京御史臺，卒，年七十二。
At Xuzhou the sorcerer Kong Zhiwen used heterodox arts to entice soldiers into rebellion. Some reported it to the transport commissioner, but he would not accept the complaint. Ju Jian had the document altered, arrested and investigated the whole clique, pardoned those misled in error, and asked the court to execute Zhiwen and the rest. When Pu Prefecture rebelled again, the capital populace panicked and scattered. Ju Jian hurried there, seized the ringleaders, and executed them. He then held a great review of troops and feasted them in reward, so that treachery could not arise. For these two matters he was promoted to Salt and Iron Commissioner. He was appointed Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, prefect of Zi and Yingtian, then transferred to Jingnan and advanced to Direct Academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Guang Prefecture, where he tiled the city walls with pottery bricks, which people found convenient. As Vice Minister of War he concurrently judged the Western Capital Censorate. He died at seventy-two.
61
張齊賢
Zhang Qixian
62
張齊賢，曹州冤句人。 生三歲，值晉亂，徙家洛陽。 孤貧力學，有遠志，慕唐李大亮之為人，故字師亮。 太祖幸西都，齊賢以布衣獻策馬前，召至行宮，齊賢以手畫地，條陳十事：曰下幷、汾、曰富民、曰封建、曰敦孝、曰舉賢、曰太學、曰籍田、曰選良吏、曰慎刑、曰懲姦。 內四說稱旨，齊賢堅執以為皆善，上怒，令武士拽出之。 及還，語太宗曰：「我幸西都，唯得一張齊賢爾。 我不欲爵之以官，異時可使輔汝為相也。」
Zhang Qixian was a native of Yuanju in Cao Prefecture. At three he encountered the turmoil of Jin, and his family moved to Luoyang. Orphaned and poor, he studied with effort and harbored far-reaching ambition. He admired the Tang figure Li Daliang and therefore took the style Shiliang. When Taizu visited the Western Capital, Qixian presented a strategy before his horse as a commoner and was summoned to the traveling palace. He traced on the ground with his hand and set forth ten items in order: subduing Bing and Fen; enriching the people; enfeoffment; encouraging filial piety; elevating the worthy; the Imperial Academy; the ceremonial plowing field; selecting good officials; cautious punishments; and punishing wickedness. Four of the proposals pleased him, but Qixian insisted that all were good. The emperor grew angry and ordered armored guards to drag him out. On returning he said to Taizong, "When I visited the Western Capital I gained only one Zhang Qixian. I do not wish to ennoble him with office now; in time he may assist you as chief councilor."
63
太宗擢進士，欲置齊賢高第，有司偶失掄選，上不悅，一榜盡與京官，於是齊賢以大理評事通判衡州。 時州鞫劫盜，論皆死，齊賢至，活其失入者五人。 自荊渚至桂州，水遞鋪夫數千戶，困於郵役，衣食多不給，論奏減其半。 四年，代還，會親征晉陽，齊賢上謁，遷秘書丞。 忻州新下，命知州事。 明年召還，改著作佐郎，直史館，改左拾遺。 冬，車駕北征，議者皆言宜速取幽薊，齊賢上疏曰：
Taizong elevated him as advanced scholar and wished to place Qixian in the highest rank, but the department by chance failed in the selection. The emperor was displeased and the entire list was given capital posts, and Qixian became Evaluator of Matters at the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent prefectural judge of Heng Prefecture. At the time the prefecture was trying robbers, and all were sentenced to death. When Qixian arrived he spared five who had been wrongly convicted. From Jingzhu to Gui Prefecture, relay courier households numbered in the thousands. Harried by postal service, they often lacked food and clothing, and he memorialized to reduce the burden by half. In the fourth year he returned on replacement of office, happened upon the emperor's personal campaign against Jinyang, and on presenting himself was promoted to Secretary Director. Xin Prefecture had just been taken, and he was ordered to manage prefectural affairs. The next year he was recalled, made Assistant Compiler, entered the Historiography Institute, and changed to Left Reminder. In winter, when the imperial carriage campaigned north, the discussants all said the You-Ji region should be taken quickly. Qixian submitted a memorial that read:
64
「方今海內一家，朝野無事。 關聖慮者，豈不以河東新平，屯兵尚眾，幽燕未下，輦運為勞？ 臣愚以為此不足慮也。 自河東初下，臣知忻州，捕得契丹納米典吏，皆云自山後轉般以授河東。 以臣料，契丹能自備軍食，則於太原非不盡力，然終為我有者，力不足也。 河東初平，人心未固，嵐、憲、忻、代未有軍砦，入寇則田牧頓失，擾邊則守備可虞。 及國家守要害，增壁壘，左控右扼，疆事甚嚴，恩信已行，民心已定，乃於雁門陽武谷來爭小利，此其智力可料而知也。 聖人舉事，動在萬全，百戰百勝，不若不戰而勝，若重之慎之，則契丹不足吞，燕薊不足取。
"At present within the seas there is one house, and court and countryside are without affairs. What occupies the sage mind—is it not because Hedong has newly been pacified, garrison troops are still numerous, You and Ji are not yet taken, and transport by imperial carriage is laborious? In your servant's foolish view this is not worth anxiety. Since Hedong was first taken, when your servant was prefect of Xin Prefecture he captured Khitan grain-supply clerks, all of whom said grain was transferred in relays from beyond the mountains to supply Hedong. By your servant's estimate, if the Khitan can supply their own army provisions, then toward Taiyuan they spare no effort—yet in the end it becomes ours because their strength is insufficient. Hedong has just been pacified and hearts are not yet firm. Lan, Xian, Xin, and Dai have no military forts. If they invade, field and pasture are suddenly lost; if the border is harassed, defense is to be feared. When the state guards strategic points, adds walls and ramparts, controls left and restrains right, and frontier affairs are very strict—when favor and trust have been carried out and popular hearts are settled—then for them to come to Yanmen's Yangwu Valley to contend for small profit, that intelligence can be calculated and known. When the sage raises an affair, his movement lies in ten thousandfold security: a hundred battles, a hundred victories—better than victory without battle. If it is treated with weight and caution, then the Khitan are not enough to swallow and You-Ji not enough to take.
65
自古疆埸之難，非盡由敵國，亦多邊吏擾而致之。 若緣邊諸砦撫御得人，但使峻壘深溝，畜力養銳，以逸自處，寧我致人，此李牧所以用趙也。 所謂擇卒不如擇將，任力不如任人。 如是則邊鄙寧，邊鄙寧則輦運減，輦運減則河北之民獲休息矣。 民獲休息，則田業增而蠶績廣，務農積穀，以實邊用。 且敵人之心固亦擇利避害，安肯投諸死地而為寇哉？
Since antiquity the difficulties of the frontier have not all come from enemy states; many also come from frontier officials harassing and causing them. If along the border the various forts are governed and controlled with the right men, so that steep ramparts and deep moats are maintained, strength is stored and keen edge nurtured, and ease is taken as one's position—better to let me strike at others—this is how Li Mu used Zhao. What is said is: choosing soldiers is not as good as choosing generals; relying on force is not as good as relying on men. If so, then the border marches are tranquil; if the border marches are tranquil, then transport is reduced; if transport is reduced, then the people of Hebei obtain rest. When the people obtain rest, field enterprise increases and silkworm work expands; devote effort to farming and accumulate grain to fill border use. Moreover the enemy's heart also chooses profit and avoids harm—how would they willingly cast themselves into deadly ground to become raiders?
66
臣聞家六合者以天下為心，豈止爭尺寸之事，角強弱之勢而已乎？ 是故聖人先本而後末，安內以養外。 人民，本也，疆土，末也。 五帝三王，未有不先根本者也。 堯、舜之道無他，在乎安民而利之爾。 民既安利，則遠人斂衽而至矣。 陛下愛民人、利天下之心，真堯、舜也。 臣慮群臣多以纖微之利，克下之術，侵苦窮民，以為功能。 至於生民疾苦，見之如不見，聞之如不聞，斂怨速尤，無大於此。 伏望慎擇通儒，分路采訪兩浙、江南、荊湖、西川、嶺南、河東，凡前日賦斂苛重者，改而正之，因而利之，使賦稅課利通濟，可經久而行，為聖朝定法； 除去舊弊，天下諸州有不便於民者，委長吏以聞。 敢循故常者，重置之法。 使天下耳目皆知陛下之心，戴陛下之惠，以德懷遠，以惠利民，則遠人之歸，可立而待也。」
Your servant has heard that one who harmonizes the six directions takes all under Heaven as heart—is it only to contend over foot and inch matters and corner strong with weak? Therefore the sage puts root first and branch after, settles within to nourish without. The people are the root; the frontier land is the branch. The Five Emperors and Three Kings—none failed to put root first. The way of Yao and Shun has nothing else—it lies in settling the people and benefiting them. Once the people are settled and benefited, distant men straighten their lapels and come. Your Majesty's heart that loves the people and benefits all under Heaven is truly that of Yao and Shun. Your servant fears that many among the ministers use minute profit and techniques for curbing subordinates, oppressing and distressing the poor people, and regard this as achievement. As for the people's hardships—seeing them as if not seen, hearing them as if not heard, gathering resentment and hastening blame—nothing is greater than this. Your servant humbly hopes that learned Confucians will be carefully chosen and sent by separate routes to investigate Liang-Zhe, Jiangnan, Jing-Hu, Xichuan, Lingnan, and Hedong. Wherever former levies and exactions were harsh, change and correct them, and thereby benefit the people, so that taxes and commercial profits are well regulated and may be carried on for long, establishing the sage dynasty's fixed law; remove old abuses. Throughout the empire, wherever any prefecture has what is not convenient for the people, let the chief official report it. Whoever dares follow the old routine—heavy penalties by law. Let all under Heaven's ears and eyes know Your Majesty's heart and bear Your Majesty's grace. With virtue embrace the distant and with favor benefit the people, then the return of distant men may be awaited standing."
67
六年，為江南西路轉運副使，冬，改右補闕，加正使。 齊賢至官，詢知饒、信、虔州土產銅、鐵、鉛、錫之所，推求前代鑄法，取饒州永平監所鑄以為定式，歲鑄五十萬貫，凡用銅八十五萬斤，鉛三十六萬斤，錫十六萬斤，詣闕面陳其事，敷奏詳確，議者不能奪。
In the sixth year he was made Vice Transport Commissioner of the Jiangnan West Circuit. In winter he was changed to Right Reminder and made chief commissioner. When Qixian reached his post he learned where Rao, Xin, and Qian produced copper, iron, lead, and tin, sought out former casting methods, and took the Yongping Directorate of Rao as the fixed model, casting five hundred thousand strings annually with eight hundred fifty thousand jin of copper, three hundred sixty thousand jin of lead, and one hundred sixty thousand jin of tin. He presented the matter at court in person; his exposition was detailed and exact, and the discussants could not overturn it.
68
先是，諸州罪人多錮送闕下，路死者十常五六。 齊賢道逢南劍、建昌、虔州所送，索牒視之，率非首犯，悉伸其冤抑。 因力言於朝，後凡送囚至京，請委強明吏慮問，不實，則罪及原問官屬。 自是江南送罪人者為減太半。
Previously, criminals from the various prefectures were mostly shackled and sent to court; of those on the road, five or six in ten commonly died. Qixian on the road encountered prisoners sent from Nanjian, Jianchang, and Qian, demanded their documents and examined them, found that for the most part they were not chief culprits, and fully redressed their wrongful oppression. Thereupon he spoke forcefully to the court. Afterward, whenever prisoners were sent to the capital, the court was asked to entrust them to strong and clear officials for reconsideration, and if not substantiated, guilt would reach the original examining officials. From this, those sending criminals from Jiangnan were reduced by more than half.
69
先是，江南諸州小民，居官地者有地房錢，吉州緣江地雖淪沒，猶納勾欄地錢，編木而浮居者名水場錢，皆前代弊政，齊賢悉論免之。
Previously, among common people of Jiangnan's prefectures, those dwelling on official land paid ground-rent for housing. In Ji Prefecture, though riverbank land had been submerged, they still paid railing-ground money. Those who wove wood and lived afloat paid water-station money. All were abuses of former dynasties, which Qixian fully memorialized to exempt.
70
初，李氏據有江南，民戶稅錢三千已上者戶出丁一人，黥面，自備器甲輸官庫，出即給之，日支糧二升，名為義軍。 既內附，皆放歸農。 至是，言者以為此輩久在行伍，不樂耕農，乞遣使選充軍伍，並其家屬送闕下。 齊賢上言：「江南義軍，例皆良民，橫遭黥配，無所逃避。 克復之後，便放歸農，久被皇風，並皆樂業。 若逐戶搜索，不無驚擾。 法貴有常，政尚清淨，前敕既放營農，不若且仍舊貫。 」齊賢居使職，勤究民弊，務行寬大，江左人思之不忘。 召還，拜樞密直學士，擢右諫議大夫、簽書樞密院事。
Initially, when the Li clan held Jiangnan, households whose tax money reached three thousand or above furnished one man per household, tattooed the face, and supplied armor and weapons themselves to deliver to the government storehouse. On going out they were issued arms, with two sheng of grain daily support, called the Righteous Army. After they submitted inward, all were released to return to farming. At this time memorialists held that this host had long been in the ranks and did not delight in farming, and begged that envoys be sent to select them to fill military companies and send their families to court. Qixian submitted, "The Jiangnan Righteous Army were in every case good common people, forcibly tattooed and assigned, with nowhere to escape. After recovery they were at once released to return to farming. Long bathed in imperial wind, all have been content in their occupations. If household by household they are searched out, there will be no lack of alarm and disturbance. Law values constancy; government esteems purity and quietness. Since the former edict already released them to camp farming, better to let the old practice stand." In his commissioner post Qixian diligently investigated the people's abuses and strove to practice leniency and breadth; the people of the Jiang left remember him without forgetting. Recalled, he was appointed Direct Academician of the Privy Council, promoted to Right Remonstrator and Commissioner of the Privy Council.
71
雍熙初，遷左諫議大夫。 三年，大舉北伐，代州楊業戰沒。 上訪近臣以策，齊賢請行，即授給事中、知代州，與部署潘美同領緣邊兵馬。 是時遼兵自湖谷入寇，薄城下，神衛都校馬正以所部列南門外，眾寡不敵，副部署盧漢贇畏懦，保壁自固。 齊賢選廂軍二千，出正之右，誓眾慷慨，一以當百，遼兵遂卻。
At the beginning of Yongxi he was transferred to Left Remonstrator. In the third year a great northern campaign was launched; Yang Ye of Dai Prefecture was killed in battle. The emperor consulted nearby ministers for strategy. Qixian requested to go and was at once made Supervising Secretary and prefect of Dai Prefecture, jointly leading frontier troops and horses with Deployment Commissioner Pan Mei. At that time Liao troops entered from Hugu Valley to raid and pressed below the city wall. Shenwei Commander Ma Zheng arrayed his command outside the south gate, but the multitude was few and could not match them. Vice Deployment Commissioner Lu Hanyun was timid and cowardly, protecting the walls and holding himself firm. Qixian selected two thousand garrison troops, went out to Zheng's right, and swore to the multitude with generous ardor—one against a hundred—and the Liao troops then withdrew.
72
先是，約潘美以幷師來會戰，無何，間使為遼人所得。 齊賢以師期既漏，且虞美眾為遼所乘。 既而美使至，云師出并州，至柏井，得密詔，東師敗績於君子館，幷之全軍不許出戰，已還州矣。 於時遼兵塞川，齊賢曰：「賊知美之來，而不知美之退。 」乃閉其使密室，中夜發兵二百，人持一幟，負一束芻，距州城西南三十里，列幟然芻。 遼兵遙見火光中有旗幟，意謂幷師至矣，駭而北走。 齊賢先伏步兵二千於土磴砦，掩擊大敗之，擒其北大王之子一人，帳前錫利一人，斬數百級，獲馬二千、器甲甚眾。 捷奏，且歸功漢贇。
Previously, it had been agreed that Pan Mei would bring Bing troops to join battle. Before long, a secret envoy was captured by the Liao. Qixian, because the army rendezvous had leaked, also feared Mei's force would be caught by the Liao. Then Mei's envoy arrived, saying the army had left Bing Prefecture and reached Baijing, received a secret edict: the eastern army had been defeated at Junzi Lodge, and Bing's entire army was not permitted to go out to battle and had already returned to the prefecture. At that time Liao troops blocked the valleys. Qixian said, "The bandits know Mei is coming but do not know Mei has withdrawn. " He then shut the envoy in a secret room. At midnight he sent out two hundred troops, each holding one banner and bearing one bundle of straw, thirty li southwest of the prefectural city, where they arrayed banners and lit the straw. From afar the Liao troops saw banners amid the firelight and thought Bing troops had arrived. Startled, they fled north. Qixian had first hidden two thousand foot soldiers at Tudeng Fort, ambushed them, and inflicted a great defeat, capturing one son of their Northern Great King, one Xili before the tent, beheading several hundred heads, and obtaining two thousand horses and very many weapons and armor. He reported victory and moreover attributed merit to Hanyun.
73
二年，置屯田，領河東制置方田都部署，入拜刑部侍郎、樞密副使。 淳化二年夏，參知政事，數月，拜吏部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。 齊賢母孫氏年八十餘，封晉國太夫人，每入謁禁中，上歎其福壽、有令子，多手詔存問，加賜與，搢紳榮之。
In the second year garrison fields were established. He headed the Hedong Directorate for Garrison Fields and Rectified Fields and entered court as Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council. In the second year of Chunhua, summer, he became Participant in Governance. Several months later he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and Concurrent Chief Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery. Qixian's mother, the Sun clan, was over eighty and was enfeoffed Lady of Jin. Whenever she entered the forbidden precincts the emperor sighed at her fortune and longevity and worthy son, often writing edicts in his own hand to inquire after her and adding gifts—officialdom regarded this as glory.
74
初，王延德與朱貽業同掌京庾，欲求補外，貽業與參政李沆有姻婭，託之以請於沆，沆為請於齊賢，齊賢以聞。 太宗以延德嘗事晉邸。 怒其不自陳而干祈執政，召見詰責。 延德、貽業皆諱不以實對，齊賢不欲累沆，獨任其責。 四年六月，罷為尚書左丞。 十月，命知定州，以母老不願往，未幾，丁內艱，水漿不入口者七日，自是日啖粥一器，終喪不食酒肉蔬果。 尋復轉禮部尚書、知河南府。 時獄有大辟將決，齊賢至，立辨而釋之。 三日，徙知永興軍。 時閣門祗候趙讚以言事得幸，提點關中芻糧，所為多豪橫。 齊賢論列其罪，卒抵於法。 俄徙襄州，移荊南，又徙安州。 逾年，加刑部尚書。
Initially, Wang Yande and Zhu Yiye jointly managed the capital granaries and wished to obtain an outside posting. Yiye had a marriage tie with Participant in Governance Li Hang and entrusted him to request it of Hang. Hang requested it of Qixian, and Qixian reported it. Taizong, because Yande had once served the Jin princely establishment, was angry that he had not stated it himself but importuned the chief councilor, summoned him, and interrogated and reproached him. Yande and Yiye both concealed and did not answer with the truth. Qixian did not wish to implicate Hang and alone bore the blame. In the sixth month of the fourth year he was demoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. In the tenth month he was ordered to be prefect of Ding Prefecture, but because his mother was old he did not wish to go. Before long he entered mourning for his mother. For seven days he would not take water or broth, and from then ate one bowl of gruel daily. Through the mourning he did not eat wine, meat, or vegetables and fruits. Soon afterward he was again made Minister of Rites and prefect of Henan Prefecture. At the time a great capital offense in the prisons was about to be decided. When Qixian arrived he immediately distinguished and released them. Three days later he was transferred to prefect of Yongxing Army. At the time Palace Gate Attendant Zhao Zan, through memorializing on affairs, had gained favor and was made intendant of Guanzhong fodder and grain. His conduct was largely overbearing. Qixian memorialized listing his crimes, and in the end he was brought to law. Soon he was transferred to Xiang Prefecture, moved to Jingnan, and again to An Prefecture. After a year he was given the additional title Vice Minister of Justice.
75
四年，李繼遷陷清遠軍，命為涇、原等州軍安撫經略使，以右司諫梁顥為之副。 齊賢上言謂：「清遠軍陷沒以來，青岡砦燒棄之後，靈武一郡，援隔勢孤，此繼遷之所覬覦而必至者也。 以事勢言之，加討則不足，防遏則有餘。 其計無他，蕃部大族首領素與繼遷有隙者，若能啖以官爵，誘以貨利，結之以恩信，而激之以利害，則山西之蕃部族帳，靡不傾心朝廷矣。 臣所領十二州軍，見二萬餘人，若緣邊料柬本城等軍，更得五萬餘人，招致蕃部，其數又逾十數萬。 但彼出則我歸，東備則西擊，使之奔走不暇，何能為我患哉？ 今靈武軍民不翅六七萬，陷於危亡之地，若繼遷來春於我兵未舉之前，發兵救援靈武，盡驅其眾，並力攻圍，則靈州孤城必難固守。 萬一失陷，賊勢益增，縱多聚甲兵，廣積財貨，亦難保必勝矣。 臣所以乞封潘羅支為六谷王而厚以金帛者，恐繼遷旦暮用兵斷彼賣馬之路也。 苟朝廷信使得達潘羅支，則泥埋等族、西南遠蕃，不難招集。 西南既禀命，而緣邊之勢張，則鄜、延、環、慶之淺蕃，原、渭、鎮戎之熟戶，自然歸化。 然後使之與對替甲兵及駐泊軍馬互為聲援，則萬山聞之，必不敢於靈州、河西頓兵矣。 萬山既退，則賀蘭蕃部亦稍稍叛繼遷矣。 若曰名器不可以假人，爵賞不可以濫及，此乃聖人為治之常道，非隨時變易之義也。」
In the fourth year Li Jiqian took Qingyuan Army. He was appointed Pacification and Frontier Commissioner of Jing, Yuan, and other prefectures, with Right Remonstrator Liang Hao as his deputy. Qixian submitted saying, "Since Qingyuan Army fell, after Qinggang Fort was burned and abandoned, the single commandery of Lingwu, cut off in support and isolated in strength—this is what Jiqian covets and is certain to reach. Speaking by the trend of affairs, to attack further is insufficient, but to defend and block is more than enough. The plan is nothing else. Among the great tribal chiefs of the Fan, those who by nature have rifts with Jiqian—if they can be fed with titles and enfeoffments, enticed with goods and profit, bound with favor and trust, and stirred with benefit and harm—then the tribal tents of the Fan in the western mountains will none fail to turn their hearts to the court. The twelve prefectural armies your servant leads presently see more than twenty thousand men. If along the border the native troops of the prefectural cities and the like are further mustered, another fifty thousand-odd may be obtained, and if Fan tribes are recruited, their number again exceeds one hundred thousand. Only when they go out we return, when they prepare east we strike west—make them run without rest. How can they become a trouble to us? Now the troops and people of Lingwu are no fewer than sixty or seventy thousand, trapped in a place of peril and death. If Jiqian next spring, before our troops are raised, sends troops to rescue Lingwu, drives out all its multitude, and with combined strength attacks and besieges, then Ling Prefecture's lone city will surely be hard to hold firm. In the event of ten thousand to one that it falls, the bandit power will increase all the more. Even if many armor and troops are gathered and wealth and goods widely stored, it will still be hard to guarantee certain victory. The reason your servant begged to enfeoff Pan Luozhi as King of the Six Valleys and reward him thickly with gold and silks is that he feared Jiqian might at any time use troops and cut off their horse-selling road. If the court's trust-envoy can reach Pan Luozhi, then the Nimi and other tribes and the distant Fan of the southwest are not hard to gather. Once the southwest has received orders and the border power is extended, then the shallow Fan of Bian, Yan, Huan, and Qing, and the registered households of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong, will naturally submit. Then have them mutually support the relief troops and stationed army horses, and when Mount Wan hears of it they will surely not dare to mass troops at Ling Prefecture and west of the river. Once Mount Wan has withdrawn, then the Helan Fan tribes will also gradually turn against Jiqian. If one says titles and vessels may not be lent to others and enfeoffments and rewards may not be lavished indiscriminately—this is the sage's constant way in governing, not the meaning of changing with the times."
76
齊賢又請調江淮、荊湘丁壯八萬以益防禦，朝議以為動搖，兼澤國人民，遠戍西鄙亦非便，計遂寢。
Qixian also requested that eight hundred thousand able-bodied men from Jianghuai and Jing-Hu be transferred to strengthen defense. Court discussion held this would cause disturbance, and moreover the people of marsh lands, sent far to garrison the western marches, was also not convenient, and the plan was then abandoned.
77
齊賢又言：「靈州斗絕一隅，當城鎮完全、磧路未梗之時，中外已言合棄，自繼遷為患已來，危困彌甚。 南去鎮戎約五百餘里，東去環州僅六七日程，如此畏途，不須攻奪，則城中之民何由而出，城中之兵何由而歸？ 欲全軍民，理須應接。 為今之計，若能增益精兵，以合西邊屯駐、對替之兵，從以原、渭、鎮戎之師，率山西熟戶從東界而入，嚴約師期，兩路交進。 設若繼遷分兵以應敵，我則乘勢而易攻。 且奔命途道，首尾難衛，千里趨利，不敗則禽。 臣謂兵鋒未交，而靈州之圍自解。 然後取靈州軍民，而置砦於蕭關、武延川險要處以僑寓之，如此則蕃漢士人之心有所依賴。 裁候平寧，卻歸舊貫，然後縱蕃漢之兵，乘時以為進退，則成功不難矣。 」時不能用。 未幾，靈武果陷。
Qixian also said, "Ling Prefecture stands isolated at a corner. When the city defenses were complete and the desert road unobstructed, within and without already spoke of abandoning it together. Since Jiqian became a calamity, peril has grown ever worse. South to Zhenrong is about five hundred-odd li; east to Huan Prefecture is only six or seven days' journey. On such a fearful road, without needing to attack and seize, how can the people within the city get out, how can the troops within the city return? To preserve army and people entirely, reason requires that they be supported. For the plan of today, if elite troops can be increased to join the western border garrisons and relief troops, accompanied by the armies of Yuan, Wei, and Zhenrong, leading registered households of the western mountains to enter from the eastern boundary, with strict agreement on army dates and two routes advancing together, Suppose Jiqian divides troops to meet the enemy—we then take advantage of the situation for easy attack. Moreover, racing orders along the road, head and tail hard to guard, rushing a thousand li for profit—if not defeated then captured. Your servant holds that before the army's edge has met, the siege of Ling Prefecture will resolve itself. Then take the troops and people of Ling Prefecture and place forts at the strategic points of Xiaoguan and Wuyan River to lodge them temporarily—thus the hearts of Fan and Han scholars and people will have something to rely on. Trim the season until peace and quiet, then return to the old practice. Afterward release Fan and Han troops and take opportunity for advance and retreat—then success is not hard." " At the time it could not be adopted. Before long Lingwu indeed fell.

閏十二月，拜右僕射、判邠州，不行，改判永興軍兼馬步軍部署。 時薛居正子惟吉妻柴氏無子早寡，盡畜其貨產及書籍論告，欲改適齊賢。 惟吉子安上訴其事，上不欲置於理，命司門員外郎張正倫就訊，柴氏所對與安上狀異。 下其事於御史，乃齊賢子太子中舍宗誨教柴氏為詞。 齊賢坐責太常卿、分司西京，宗誨貶海州別駕。
In the intercalary twelfth month he was appointed Right Vice Director and judge of Bin Prefecture. He did not go and was changed to judge of Yongxing Army concurrently with Commissioner of Cavalry and Infantry. At the time Xue Juzheng's son Weiji's wife, the Chai clan, was without a son and widowed early. She stored all her property and books and memorialized accusations, wishing to remarry Qixian. Weiji's son An appealed the matter. The emperor did not wish to place it in the law courts and ordered Vice Director of the Gate Office Zhang Zhenglun to conduct an inquiry on the spot. The Chai clan's answers differed from An's memorial. The matter was sent down to the censorate—it was Qixian's son, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household Zonghui, who had taught the Chai clan her words. Qixian was punished by demotion to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and commissioner in the Western Capital, and Zonghui was demoted to Assistant Prefect of Haizhou.

景德初，起為兵部尚書、知青州。 上幸澶淵，命兼青、淄、濰州安撫使。 二年，改吏部尚書。 上疏言曰：「臣在先朝，常憂靈、夏，兩鎮終為繼遷並吞，言事者以臣所慮為太過，略舉既往之事以明本末。 當時臣下皆以繼遷只是懷戀父祖舊地，別無他心，先帝與以銀州廉察，庶滿其意。 爾後攻劫不已，直至降麟、府州界八部族蕃酋，又脅制賀蘭山下帳族，言事者猶謂封獎未厚。 洎陛下賜以銀、夏土壤，寵以節旄，自此姦威愈滋，逆志尤暴。 屢斷靈州糧路，復撓緣邊城池，數年之間，靈州終為吞噬。 當靈池、清遠軍垂欲陷沒，臣方受經略之命。 臣思繼遷須是得一兩處強大蕃族與之為敵，此乃以蠻夷攻蠻夷，古今之上策也。 遂請以六谷名目封潘羅支，俾其展效。 其時近臣所見，全與臣謀不同，多為沮撓。 及繼遷為潘羅支射殺，邊患謂可少息。 今其子德明依前攻劫，析逋遊龍缽等盡在部下，其志又似不小。 臣慮德明乘大駕東幸之際，去攻六谷，則瓜、沙、甘、肅、于闐諸處漸為控制矣。 向使潘羅支尚在，則德明未足為虞； 今潘羅支已亡，廝鐸督恐非其敵。 望委大臣經制其事。」
At the beginning of Jingde he was raised as Vice Minister of War and prefect of Qing Prefecture. When the emperor visited Chanyuan he was ordered concurrently to be Pacification Commissioner of Qing, Zi, and Wei prefectures. In the second year he was changed to Minister of Personnel. Zhang Qixian submitted a memorial that read: "In the previous reign I often feared that Lingzhou and Xiazhou would ultimately be absorbed by Li Jiqian. Officials who addressed policy matters thought my concern excessive. I will briefly recount what has already happened to show how matters unfolded from start to finish." At the time every official maintained that Jiqian wanted only his ancestors' former lands and harbored no wider ambition. The late emperor gave him the Yinzhou inspectorate, hoping that would satisfy him. After that he raided without cease, subduing the eight tribal chiefs along the Linzhou-Fuzhou frontier and coercing the tent peoples below Helan Mountain. Memorialists still argued that his titles and rewards had not been generous enough. Once Your Majesty granted him Yinzhou and Xiazhou and invested him with a commissioner's insignia, his treachery grew only stronger and his defiance far fiercer. He repeatedly cut Lingzhou's supply lines and harassed border towns until, within a few years, the prefecture fell entirely into his hands. When Lingchi and the Qingyuan garrison were on the brink of collapse, I had just been assigned to oversee the frontier. I reasoned that Jiqian could be checked only if one or two powerful tribal groups were set against him—the classic strategy of pitting barbarian against barbarian. I therefore asked that Pan Luozhi be enfeoffed under the Six Valleys title so that he could act against Jiqian. Courtiers close to the throne saw things altogether differently and largely blocked the proposal. After Pan Luozhi killed Jiqian with an arrow, the frontier crisis was thought to ease at last. Now his son Deming raids as before. Tribal leaders such as Xibo and Youlongbo are all in his following, and his designs again appear ambitious. I fear that while the imperial progress is in the east, Deming may strike at the Six Valleys and then gradually bring Guazhou, Shazhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Khotan, and the rest under his control. Had Pan Luozhi still lived, Deming would scarcely have been cause for alarm; but Pan Luozhi is dead, and Sieduoge is probably no match for him. I beg that senior ministers be assigned to handle the matter."

從東封還，復拜右僕射。 時建玉清昭應宮，齊賢言繪畫符瑞，有損謙德，又違奉天之意，屢請罷其役。
After returning from the eastern Fengshan rites, he was again appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat. While the Jade Pure Palace of Manifest Response was under construction, Qixian argued that painting omens and prodigies would diminish modest virtue and violate the spirit of honoring Heaven. He repeatedly asked that the project be stopped.

三年，出判河陽，從祀汾陰還，進左僕射。 五年，代還，請老，以司空致仕。 入辭便坐，方拜而仆，上遽止之，許二子扶掖升殿，命益坐茵為三。
In the third year he was posted as administrative prefect of Heyang. After accompanying the Fengyin sacrifice he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat. In the fifth year his successor arrived; he asked to retire and was permitted to withdraw with the rank of Minister of Works. When he came in to bid farewell at the Informal Audience, he had barely begun to bow when he fell. The emperor quickly stopped him, allowed his two sons to help him onto the dais, and ordered a third cushion placed for him to sit on.

歸洛，得裴度午橋莊，有池榭松竹之盛，日與親舊觴詠其間，意甚曠適。 七年夏，薨，年七十二。 贈司徒，諡文定。
Back in Luoyang he acquired Pei Du's Noon Bridge estate, with its fine pools, pavilions, pines, and bamboo. There he drank and wrote poetry daily with relatives and old friends, his spirit altogether serene and free. In the seventh year, summer, he died at seventy-two. He was posthumously made Minister of Education and given the posthumous title Wending, "Cultivated and Settled."

齊賢姿儀豐碩，議論慷慨，有大略，以致君自負。 留心刑獄，多所全活。 喜提獎寒雋。 少時家貧，父死無以為葬，河南縣吏為辦其事，齊賢深德之，事以兄禮，雖貴不替也。 仲兄昭度嘗授齊賢經，及卒，表贈光祿寺丞。 又嘗依太子少師李肅家，肅死，為營葬事，歲時祭之。 趙普嘗薦齊賢於太宗，未用，普即具前列事，以謂：「陛下若進齊賢，則齊賢他日感恩，更過於此。 」上大悅，遂大用。 种放之起，齊賢所薦也。 齊賢四踐兩府，九居八座，以三公就第，康寧福壽，時罕其比。 居相日，數起大獄，又與寇準相傾，人或以此少之。
Qixian was imposing in stature and voice, spoke with force and breadth, and held to a grand design, confident that he could guide his sovereign to success. He took a close interest in criminal justice and saved many from execution. He delighted in promoting talented men of humble origin. In youth his family was poor. When his father died he could not afford a burial until a clerk of Henan County arranged it. Qixian never forgot the debt and treated the man as an elder brother, a courtesy he kept even at the height of his career. His elder brother Zhaodu had once taught him the classics. When Zhaodu died, Qixian memorialized for him a posthumous appointment as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He had also once lived under the roof of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Li Su. When Su died, Qixian arranged his burial and made seasonal offerings thereafter. Zhao Pu once recommended Qixian to Emperor Taizong, but the appointment was not made. Pu then laid out in full what he had done for Qixian and said, "If Your Majesty promotes Qixian now, his gratitude one day will exceed even this." The emperor was greatly pleased and thereafter gave him full employment. Chong Fang's rise to prominence came through Qixian's recommendation. Qixian served four times in the Two Departments, nine times among the Eight Seats, and retired home with the rank of the Three Excellencies—healthy, secure, blessed, and long-lived, a combination rare in his age. As chief minister he repeatedly opened major prosecutions and also feuded with Kou Zhun, and some held that against him.

齊賢諸子皆能有立：宗信，內殿崇班； 宗理，大理寺丞； 宗諒，殿中丞； 宗簡，閣門祗候； 宗訥，太子中舍； 宗禮最賢，雖累資登朝，而畏羈束，故多居田里。
All of Qixian's sons made their way in the world: Zongxin became an Inner Hall Honored Escort; Zongli, Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review; Zongliang, Director Within the Hall; Zongjian, Gate Attendant of the Imperial Portal; Zongne, Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household; Zongli was the most worthy of them. Though seniority eventually brought him to court, he disliked constraint and mostly lived in the countryside.

子宗誨
Son: Zonghui
86
宗誨，字習之，齊賢第二子也。 少喜學兵法，陰陽、象緯之書無不通究。 以父蔭為秘書省正字，遷至太子中舍，貶海州別駕。 嘗通判河陽，徙知富順監。 會夷人斗郎春叛，群獠皆騷動，宗誨將郡兵攻破之。 擢開封府判官、三司度支勾院。 宗誨在開封日，御史王沿劾其嗜酒廢事，及為河北轉運使，乃發沿居喪假官舟賈販，朝論惡之。 會以調發擾民，徙知徐州。 累遷太常少卿，後為永興軍兵馬鈐轄，又徙鄜延路兼知鄜州。 元昊寇延安，劉平、石元孫敗沒，鈐轄黃德和遁還，延州不納，又走鄜州。 宗誨曰：「軍奔將無所歸，激之則為亂矣。 」乃納之，拘德和以聞。 是時鄜城不完，且無備，傳言寇兵至，人心不安。 宗誨乃嚴斥候，籍入而禁出，使老幼倂力守禦之，敵亦自引去。 領興州防禦使，復徙永興鈐轄兼知邠州，以秘書監致仕。
Zonghui, styled Xizhi, was Qixian's second son. As a youth he loved military science and mastered works on cosmology, divination, and astronomy alike. Through his father's privilege he entered service as a Secretariat corrector, rose to Rectifier of the Heir Apparent's Household, and was demoted to Vice Prefect of Haizhou. He once served as transit judge of Heyang and was later transferred to head the Fushun Directorate. When the Yi leader Doulangchun rebelled and tribal groups across the region rose in unrest, Zonghui led prefectural troops and broke the rebellion. He was promoted to administrative judge of the Kaifeng prefectural court and to the audit office of the Three Departments' revenue section. While Zonghui was in Kaifeng, Censor Wang Yan impeached him for drinking to excess and neglecting his duties. Once Zonghui became Hebei transport commissioner, he exposed Yan's use of an official boat for trade during mourning, and court opinion turned against him. When his requisitions burdened the people, he was transferred to administer Xuzhou. He rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then served as military controller of Yongxing Army, and was later transferred to the Yan-Yan circuit while also governing Yan Prefecture. When Yuanhao attacked Yan'an, Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated and lost. Military Controller Huang Dehe fled back, but Yanzhou refused him entry, so he fled on to Yan Prefecture. Zonghui said, "When routed troops have nowhere to go, a general with no refuge, if you push him further you will breed mutiny." He therefore admitted Dehe, detained him, and reported the matter to the court. At the time the walls of Yan were unfinished and the city unprepared. Rumors of approaching raiders unsettled the populace. Zonghui tightened scouting, registered those entering and barred departures, and rallied young and old to defend together. The enemy withdrew on their own. He served as Defender of Xing Prefecture, was again made military controller of Yongxing while also governing Bin Prefecture, and retired with the rank of Director of the Secretariat.

嘗事干謁，其子曰：「昔賀秘監以道士服東歸會稽，明皇賜以鑒湖，以為休老之地。 今洛下雖無鑒湖，而嵩、少、伊，天下佳處，雖非朝廷所賜，皆閑逸之人所有爾。 大人盍衣羽服以優遊，何必更事請謁乎？ 」宗誨曰：「吾作白頭老監秘書而眠，何以賀老流沙之服為哉？ 」時以為名言。
He had once gone about seeking favors. His son said, "Long ago Junior Mentor He Zhizhang, dressed as a Daoist, returned east to Kuaiji, and Emperor Xuanzong gave him Mirror Lake as a place to spend his old age." Luoyang may lack Mirror Lake, but Mount Song, Mount Shao, and the Yi River are among the finest places under Heaven. Though the court did not grant them, they belong to those who live at ease. Why not put on feathered robes and wander freely? Why go on begging audiences and favors?" Zonghui replied, "I am content to sleep out my days as a white-haired supervising secretary. What need have I for Old He's flowing robes from the western desert?" At the time this was regarded as a memorable saying.

He had two sons. Zigao, styled Shumo, won an early name for talent without arrogance, and people were glad to keep his company. 子憲，字彥章，以蔭將作監主簿，以獻文賜同進士出身，累遷尚書刑部郎中、知光化軍。 戍卒逐其帥韓綱，餘黨作亂，子憲招降之。 征稅重，人多逋負，子憲奏除之。 歷太常少卿、三司鹽鐵判官、直史館、知洪州。 遷右諫議大夫、知桂州，不赴，御史劾之，降秘書監。 復為光祿卿，加直秘閣、知廬州，遷秘書監，累職徙揚州，卒。
Zixian, styled Yanzhang, entered service by privilege as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works. A literary submission earned him jinshi status by imperial favor. He rose to Director in the Ministry of Justice's Penal Section and governed Guanghua Army. The garrison expelled its commander Han Gang, and the remaining mutineers rose in disorder until Zixian persuaded them to surrender. Taxes were heavy and many fell into arrears; Zixian memorialized to have them remitted. He served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, salt-and-iron judge in the Three Departments, historian on duty in the Historiography Institute, and prefect of Hongzhou. 賈黃中
Jia Huangzhong
92
賈黃中，字媧民，滄州南皮人，唐相耽四世孫。 父玭，字仲寶，晉天福三年進士，解褐。 宋初，為刑部郎中，終水部員外郎、知浚儀縣，年七十卒。 玭嚴毅，善教子，士大夫子弟來謁，必諄諄誨誘之。 初，通判鎮州，葬鄉黨群從之未葬者十五喪，孤貧不自給者，咸教育而婚嫁之。
Jia Huangzhong, styled Guamin, was a native of Nanpi in Cangzhou, a fourth-generation descendant of the Tang chief minister Jia Dan. His father Bin, styled Zhongbao, passed the jinshi examination in the third year of the Later Jin Tianfu era and entered government service. Early in the Song he served as Director in the Ministry of Justice's Penal Section and ended his career as Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Water Section and magistrate of Junyi County, dying at seventy. Bin was stern and disciplined, skilled at raising sons. Whenever the sons of scholar-officials called on him, he earnestly instructed and guided them. Earlier, as transit judge of Zhenzhou, he buried fifteen kinsmen of his village and clan who had gone unburied, and for orphans and the poor who could not support themselves he provided education and arranged marriages.
93
黃中幼聰悟，方五歲，比每旦令正立，展書卷比之，謂之「等身書」，課其誦讀。 六歲舉童子科，七歲能屬文，觸類賦詠。 父常令蔬食，曰：「俟業成，乃得食肉。 」十五舉進士，授校書郎、集賢校理，遷著作佐郎、直史館。
Huangzhong was clever as a child. At five, each morning his father made him stand upright, unrolled a scroll to his height, called it a "body-length book," and drilled him in recitation. At six he passed the Youth Examination; at seven he could write prose and compose verse on any theme set before him. His father often fed him only vegetables, saying, "When your studies are finished, you may eat meat." At fifteen he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator and collating editor in the Academy for Worthies, and was later made Assistant Compiler with duty in the Historiography Institute.

建隆三年，遷左拾遺，歷左補闕。 開寶八年，通判定州，判太常禮院。 黃中多識典故，每詳定禮文，損益得中，號為稱職。
In the third year of the Jianlong era he was made Left Reminder and later served as Left Supplementation Censor. In the eighth year of the Kaibao era he served as transit judge of Dingzhou and concurrently oversaw the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Rites Office. Huangzhong knew a great store of precedent. Whenever he revised ritual texts his adjustments struck the right balance, and he was praised as thoroughly competent.
