嶺南平，以黃中為采訪使，廉直平恕，遠人便之。 還奏利害數十事，皆稱旨。 會克江表，選知宣州。 歲饑，民多為盜，黃中出己奉造糜粥，賴全活者以千數，仍設法弭盜，因悉解去。
After Lingnan was pacified, Huangzhong was made investigation commissioner. Honest, even-handed, and forgiving, he made life easier for the peoples of the far south. On his return he memorialized on dozens of matters of policy, all of which met with imperial approval. When the lower Yangzi region was conquered, he was chosen to govern Xuanzhou. In a year of famine many turned to banditry. Huangzhong spent his own salary to provide gruel, saving thousands of lives, then devised measures to end the unrest and released the offenders.
96
太宗即位，遷禮部員外郎。 太平興國二年，知昇州。 時金陵初附，黃中為政簡易，部內甚治。 一日，案行府署中，見一室扃鑰甚固，命發視之，得金寶數十匱，計直數百萬，乃李氏宮閣中遺物也，即表上之。 上覽表謂侍臣曰：「非黃中廉恪，則亡國之寶，將汙法而害人矣。 」賜錢三十萬。 丁父憂，起復視事。 五年，召歸闕。
When Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, Huangzhong was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites. In the second year of the Taiping Xingguo era he was made prefect of Shengzhou. Jinling had only recently submitted, and Huangzhong governed with simplicity and ease until his jurisdiction was thoroughly well ordered. One day, touring the prefectural offices, he found a room locked unusually tight. When he had it opened, he discovered dozens of chests of gold and jewels worth millions—the hoarded relics of the Li palace—and at once reported them to the throne. Reading the memorial, the emperor told his attendants, "Had Huangzhong not been so upright and restrained, the treasures of a fallen dynasty would have corrupted the law and harmed the people." Huangzhong was rewarded with three hundred thousand cash. After his father's death he entered mourning, then was recalled to office before the mourning period ended. In the fifth year he was summoned back to the capital.
97
有薦黃中文學高第，召試中書，拜駕部員外郎、知制誥。 八年，與宋白、呂蒙正等同知貢舉，遷司封郎中，充翰林學士。 雍熙二年，又知貢舉，俄掌吏部選。 端拱初，加中書舍人。 二年，兼史館修撰。 凡再典貢部，多柬拔寒俊，除擬官吏，品藻精當。 淳化二年秋，與李沆並拜給事中、參知政事。 太宗召見其母王氏，命坐，謂曰：「教子如是，真孟母矣。 」作詩以賜之，頒賜甚厚。
When someone recommended Huangzhong for outstanding literary learning, he was examined in the Secretariat and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of War's Chariots Section with duty drafting edicts. In the eighth year he served with Song Bai, Lü Mengzheng, and others as co-supervisor of the civil examinations, was made Director in the Ministry of Rites' Seals Section, and appointed Hanlin Academician. In the second year of the Yongxi era he again supervised the examinations and soon took charge of appointments in the Ministry of Personnel. At the beginning of the Duangong era he was additionally appointed Secretariat Drafter. In the second year he was also made compiler in the Historiography Institute. Twice he presided over the examinations and largely advanced talented men of humble origin. In recommending officials his judgments were consistently apt. In the autumn of the second year of the Chunhua era he and Li Hang were jointly appointed Supervising Attendant and Vice Grand Councilor. Emperor Taizong summoned his mother, Lady Wang, had her seated, and said, "To raise a son like this is truly the work of Mencius's mother." He composed a poem for her and bestowed lavish gifts besides.
98
黃中素重呂端為人，屬端出鎮襄陽，黃中力薦於上，因留為樞密直學士，遂參知政事。 當世文行之士，多黃中所薦引，而未嘗言，人莫之知也。 然畏慎過甚，中書政事頗留不決。
Huangzhong had long admired Lü Duan's character. When Duan was posted to guard Xiangyang, Huangzhong strongly recommended him to the throne, and Duan was kept at court as direct academician in the Bureau of Military Affairs and later made Vice Grand Councilor. Many leading scholars and men of integrity of the age owed their advancement to Huangzhong, yet he never spoke of it, and few knew. Yet he was excessively cautious, and Secretariat business often lingered unresolved.
99
四年冬，與沆並罷守本官。 明年，知襄州，上言母老乞留京，改知澶州。 辭日，上戒之曰：「夫小心翼翼，君臣皆當然； 若太過，則失大臣之體。 」黃中頓首謝。 上因謂侍臣曰：「朕嘗念其母有賢德，七十餘年未覺老，每與之語，甚明敏。 黃中終日憂畏，必先其母老矣。 」因目參知政事蘇易簡曰：「易簡之母亦如之。 自古賢母不可多得。 」易簡前謝曰：「陛下以孝治天下，獎及人親，臣實何人，膺茲榮遇。」
In the winter of the fourth year he and Li Hang were dismissed together and retained only their original ranks. The following year he was made prefect of Xiangzhou, but memorialized that his mother was elderly and begged to remain near the capital; he was reassigned to Chanzhou instead. On the day he took leave, the emperor admonished him, saying, "Caution in small things is proper for ruler and subject alike; but taken too far it ceases to suit a great minister." Huangzhong kowtowed in thanks. The emperor then told his attendants, "I have often thought how worthy his mother is. Though past seventy, she seems scarcely aged, and whenever I speak with her she is remarkably sharp." Huangzhong lives in constant anxiety—no doubt because he fears for his aging mother." " He then looked at Vice Grand Councilor Su Yijian and said, "Yijian's mother is the same." Worthy mothers have always been rare. Yijian stepped forward and replied, "Your Majesty governs the realm through filial piety and honors even others' parents. What am I, that I should receive such grace?"
100
至道初，黃中遘疾，詔令歸闕。 會建儲宮，擇大臣有德望者為賓友，黃中在選中。 以久疾，改命李至、李沆兼賓客，黃中亦特拜禮部侍郎，代至兼秘書監。 黃中素嗜文籍，既居內閣，甚以為慰。
At the beginning of the Zhidao era Huangzhong fell ill, and an edict ordered him back to the capital. When the heir apparent's household was established, eminent ministers were chosen as his tutors, and Huangzhong was among them. Because of his prolonged illness, Li Zhi and Li Hang were appointed joint tutors instead. Huangzhong was specially made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and replaced Zhi as concurrent Director of the Secretariat. Huangzhong had always loved books, and once he held office in the inner cabinet he found the post a great comfort.
101
二年，以疾卒，年五十六，其母尚無恙，卒如上言。 贈禮部尚書。 上聞其素貧，別賜錢三十萬。 既葬，其母入謝，又賜白金三百兩。 上謂之曰：「勿以諸孫為念，朕當不忘也。」
In the second year he died of illness at fifty-six. His mother was still in good health, and he died as he had foretold. He was posthumously made Minister of Rites. Learning that he had always been poor, the emperor granted him an additional three hundred thousand cash. After the funeral his mother came to court to give thanks and received another three hundred taels of silver. The emperor told her, "Do not worry for your grandsons; I shall not forget them."
102
黃中端謹，能守家法，廉白無私。 多知臺閣故事，談論亹亹，聽者忘倦焉。 在翰林日，太宗召見，訪以時政得失，黃中但言：「臣職典書詔，思不出位，軍國政事，非臣所知。 」上益重之，以為謹厚。 及知政事，卒無所建明，時論不之許。 有文集三十卷。
Huangzhong was decorous and disciplined, upheld his family's standards, and was scrupulously honest and impartial. He knew a great store of court precedent and could talk at length without wearying his listeners. While serving in the Hanlin Academy, Emperor Taizong summoned him and asked about current policy. Huangzhong replied only, "My duty is to draft edicts; my thoughts do not stray beyond my office. Military and state affairs are not for me to judge." The emperor valued him all the more for his restraint and integrity. Once he entered the chief council, however, he offered no notable initiatives, and contemporary opinion did not regard him favorably. He left a collected works in thirty juan.
103
子守謙，雍熙二年進士； 守正，獻文召試，賜進士第，後為虞部員外郎； 守約，國子博士； 守文，殿中丞； 守訥，右讚善大夫。
His son Shouqian passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Yongxi era; Shouzheng, after submitting a literary work for examination, was granted jinshi status and later became Vice Director in the Ministry of War's Chariots Section; Shouyue, Erudite of the Directorate of Education; Shouwen, Director Within the Hall; Shoune, Right Mentor Grandee.
104
論曰：《詩》云：「允也天子，降予卿士，實為阿衡，實左右商王。 」言有是君則有是臣，有是臣則足以相是君也。 太宗勵精庶政，注意輔相，以昉舊德，亟加進用，繼擢蒙正、齊賢，迭居相位； 復進黃中，俾參大政。 而四臣者將順德美，修明庶政，以致承平之治，可謂君臣各盡其道者矣。 君子謂李昉為多遜所毀而不校，蒙正為張紳所汙而不辨，齊賢為同列所累而不言，黃中多所薦引而不有其功，此固人之所難也。 而況四臣者皆賢宰輔，又能進退有禮，皆以善終，非盛德君子，其孰能與於斯？
The commentators say: The Book of Songs declares, "Surely the Son of Heaven sends down ministers and grandees to serve as Chief Regulator and to stand at the side of the King of Shang." This means that such a ruler draws forth such ministers, and such ministers are fit to assist such a ruler. Emperor Taizong threw himself into governance and chose his chief ministers with care. He quickly advanced Li Fang for his long service, then raised Lü Mengzheng and Zhang Qixian in turn to the chief ministership; and later advanced Jia Huangzhong to share in high policy. These four ministers followed their sovereign's virtue, refined ordinary administration, and helped bring about an age of peace—a case in which ruler and ministers each fulfilled their proper roles. Men of judgment observed that Li Fang was slandered by Li Duoxun yet did not answer back, that Lü Mengzheng was maligned by Zhang Shen yet did not defend himself, that Zhang Qixian was burdened by colleagues yet kept silent, and that Jia Huangzhong advanced many men yet claimed no credit—qualities that are genuinely hard to achieve. Moreover, all four were worthy chief ministers who advanced and withdrew with propriety and ended their lives well. Without men of great virtue, who could have matched them?
